newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on low turnover.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on low turnover.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Friday, but turnover was low as investors were restrained by poor liquidity, analysts said.
The all share index closed 2.3 points up at 730.2. Price gains led declines by 32 to 22. Lion Brewery LION.CM rose one rupee to 38.50, Development Finance five to 270.
"Prices are still at good levels at which to buy," said Derendra Abayaratna of Century Growth Fund. "The problem is to find shares."
Sellers are holding back in the hope of better prices, brokers said.
Stocks are seen rising on good growth expectations and falling fixed income rates, brokers said.
Fixed incomes have fallen on improved money supply, after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios by three percent, they said.
Analysts expect the index to continue to move up gradually next week, as it reacts to first quarter 1997 corporate results.
"The hectic upward movements of the first quarter, when the index rose over 20 percent on improved sentiment, is finished," said Nanda Nair, head of research at brokerage John Keells.
"The market should now move in a more rational manner as it reacts to fundamentals," he said.
